content.text: {"deal_state_line":"Waiting on customer: Ben deferred next steps with no date, Helen needs internal alignment and has migration worries, and CFO Farah has not been engaged.","customer_value_line":"Ben's stated outcome: store managers know by mid afternoon what to reorder, including ship from store orders, instead of finding out from an empty shelf the next morning; the merged model on a five minute refresh addressed that in the sandbox.","what_we_validated":["Store sales and ship from store orders merged in one model, updated every five minutes","SKU match via the customer crosswalk: about four percent of rows unmatched, mostly discontinued items, listed in an exceptions table","Per store and SKU replenishment projection to reorder point, shown by mid afternoon","Alerts to store managers in Teams, routable to district managers using the district field in the store table","Scale: sandbox ran twenty stores; Tom said he is comfortable with 640 stores since the merge runs per store in parallel"],"integration_patterns":["Connectors for the POS system and the ecommerce database; Apex helps build the first models; customer owns the SKU crosswalk","POS extracts unchanged; Apex reads the files where they land today","Backfill about two years of POS history in the current format; older format only if the model needs it","Teams alerts to store managers, with district routing"],"objections_and_answers":["Helen, implementation effort and team capacity (voiced as timing; past migration took four months and cost two engineers): Tom said connectors and first models are done with her team and crosswalk ownership stays with the customer, but gave no weeks or effort estimate.
